facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs' Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 lists in its footprint 242 health facilities equipped with online birth registration systems, where parents can register a child before the mother is discharged; it gives no date for the count, so the plan's date is used.
facts.system: online birth registration systems at health facilities

facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs' Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 counts 242 health facilities equipped with online birth registration systems, beside 325 front offices that render birth and death registration and 220 mobile offices; it states facilities equipped, not facilities registering, and gives no date, so the plan's date is used.
facts.system: online birth registration systems at health facilities

facts.fact: The Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 sets as its 2026/27 target one civic process digitalised, the registration of births at 0-30 days and 31 days to 1 year including non-citizens, to be deployed in medical facilities, with quarterly milestones; late birth registration and marriage follow in 2027/28 and death registration in 2028/29, and the 2025/26 work is given as reviewing the requirement specifications for automated birth registration.

The Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 places the output 'civic processes digitalised', starting with birth registration, with the Department of Home Affairs' Information Services branch, whose Deputy Director-General approves the functional requirement specifications in the first quarter.

The Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 carries the digitalisation of civic processes as an output of Programme 1, Administration, and states that the budget for modernising the department sits mainly under the Administration Programme.
